subject: chemical
audience: FE Chemical candidates and chemical engineering students
title: The Compressor That Heated the Gas to 446 K
featured_title: THE COMPRESSOR THAT HEATED THE GAS TO 446 K

presentation.challenge: No heater was attached, yet adiabatic reversible compression raised the ideal-gas temperature from 300 K to about 446 K.

practice.primary_question: Why does an ideal gas heat up during isentropic compression even when no heat is added?
practice.typical_exam_trap: Assuming adiabatic compression means constant temperature because heat transfer is zero.

case_dna.target_misconception: An adiabatic ideal-gas compressor must keep the gas temperature constant because no heat is transferred.
case_dna.why_plausible: Adiabatic means Q=0, which can be confused with no energy change.
case_dna.contradicting_evidence: For reversible adiabatic compression of an ideal gas, T2/T1=(P2/P1)^((k-1)/k). From 100 to 400 kPa at T1=300 K with k=1.4, T2≈445.8 K.
case_dna.corrected_model: Adiabatic does not mean isothermal. Compressor work raises internal energy and temperature.

problem_statement: An ideal gas enters a reversible adiabatic compressor at 100 kPa and 300 K and exits at 400 kPa. Use k=1.40. A note predicts 300 K outlet temperature because the compressor is adiabatic. Determine the isentropic outlet temperature and identify the energy misconception.

gates.label: Incident
gates.heading: No heat entered. The gas still became hotter.
gates.prompt: What process relation links pressure and temperature for an ideal-gas isentropic compression?

options.label: Use T2/T1=(P2/P1)^((k-1)/k)
options.reason: This is the ideal-gas relation for a reversible adiabatic process.

options.label: Set T2=T1 because Q=0
options.reason: Adiabatic and isothermal are different process constraints.

options.label: Use T2/T1=P1/P2
options.reason: That is not the isentropic ideal-gas relation.

gates.label: Experiment
gates.heading: Compress the gas
gates.result: The ideal isentropic outlet temperature is about 446 K.

gates.label: Evidence
gates.heading: Adiabatic compression can still increase internal energy

cards.text: Adiabatic means zero heat transfer, not zero work.
The compressor does work on the gas.
The isentropic relation predicts T2≈446 K.

claims.label: C2
claims.reason: Adiabatic does imply zero heat transfer.

claims.label: C3
claims.reason: Zero heat transfer does not imply zero compressor work or constant temperature.

evidence_choices.label: T2=300×4^(0.4/1.4)≈445.8 K
evidence_choices.reason: This is the isentropic ideal-gas result.

correction.template: The ideal isentropic outlet temperature is about {temperature} K.

gates.label: Design Fix
gates.heading: Reduce compressor discharge temperature
gates.constraint: Keep the same overall pressure ratio.

options.label: Use multistage compression with intercooling
options.reason: Intercooling removes heat between stages and can reduce discharge temperature and work.

options.label: Increase the pressure ratio further in one stage
options.reason: That raises the ideal discharge temperature.

options.label: Keep the same process but call it isothermal
options.reason: Changing the label does not change the thermodynamic path.

gates.label: Transfer
gates.heading: Apply isentropic temperature scaling
gates.prompt: For the same gas and inlet temperature, what happens to T2 if the pressure ratio increases?

options.label: T2 increases
options.reason: The pressure ratio is raised to a positive exponent.

options.label: T2 decreases
options.reason: That contradicts the isentropic compression relation.

options.label: T2 stays constant
options.reason: That would describe isothermal behavior, not isentropic compression.

gates.explanation: For an ideal gas with k>1, isentropic compression raises temperature as pressure ratio increases.

gates.label: Sign Off
gates.heading: Sign off the compression model
gates.confirmation: I confirm that an adiabatic compressor can raise gas temperature because shaft work changes the gas energy.

items.label: What was missed
items.value: Compressor shaft work raises gas energy.

items.label: Corrected model
items.value: Use the isentropic ideal-gas pressure-temperature relation for the stated process.

seo.seo_title: Isentropic Compression Temperature: 300 K to 446 K | FE E-065
seo.meta_description: Solve FE Chemical Case E-065: ideal-gas compression from 100 to 400 kPa at k=1.4 raises temperature from 300 K to about 446 K.
seo.excerpt: Adiabatic does not mean constant temperature. Compressor work can heat a gas even when Q=0.
seo.direct_answer: For a reversible adiabatic ideal-gas compression, T2/T1=(P2/P1)^((k-1)/k). With a pressure ratio of 4, T1=300 K, and k=1.4, T2≈445.8 K.

faqs.q: Does adiabatic compression keep temperature constant?
faqs.a: No. Adiabatic means no heat transfer; compressor work can increase temperature.
